title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD SPECIAL MEETING
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board called a special meeting Monday afternoon at 4:00 to wrap up some unfinished business from last week’s regular meeting.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order, and trustees quickly got to work. The main reason for the special session was to finalize contract changes for the village’s trash vendor, DBS Disposal. Damon Simmons told trustees last week that he is selling the business to Steve Stortzum of Louisville. Simmons asked the board to approve a revised contract that removes his name and adds Stortzum. Services will stay exactly the same, and Stortzum pledged he will be available through the business phone number. Trustees made a motion to approve the updated contract language, and they passed it unanimously.

Trustees also learned last week that the village is now down one service vehicle, and the remaining one is nearing the end of its useful life. Mayor Delonshaw presented a proposal from Eagleson Automotive in Olney. The Board is now considering whether to purchase one replacement vehicle or add a second vehicle. The mayor asked trustees to compare options from other local dealers, including regular cab and crew cab models. The board tabled the issue until a future meeting so members can make better comparisons.

The meeting moved along quickly until trustees took up the Appropriations Ordinance. Village Attorney Barry Bright explained that the figures in the ordinance are estimates of what the village may need to spend in the coming year. He reminded the board that the document serves as a wish list rather than an actual budget or automatic approval to spend money. Trustees must still vote on any specific expenditure at a later date.  Trustee Sue Lindeman said she understands spending must rise over time, but she questioned why this year’s ordinance runs one million dollars higher than last year’s. Trustees Jim Duff and Larry Phillips also pushed back, saying the village needs to rein in spending. After some back-and-forth discussion, Trustee Beth Prosser, attending remotely, helped clarify the process. Phillips and Duff agreed with her explanation. Trustee Travis Strasbaugh then made a motion to approve the ordinance. Prosser seconded it, and the board passed the measure four-to-one, with Lindeman voting no.

Next, trustees discussed the tax levy for the new year. Attorney Bright explained the village can raise the levy by up to 4.9 percent without triggering extra requirements. If they raise it by 5 percent or more, they must advertise the hearing in the newspaper at a cost of over $600 and hold a truth-in-taxation hearing so taxpayers can speak their mind. Since action isn’t required until later this year, the board decided to table the issue until September.

Another lengthy discussion focused on action the board took last week to help Ali Hilderbrand move her business, Ali’s Beauty Barn, to Clay City behind Casey’s. Attorney Bright said the previous action was improper. Trustees had agreed to sell her a lot for just ten dollars and cover utility installation. Bright noted the village last sold a lot at that price for residential use, not commercial. The board voted to rescind last week’s decision and looked for other ways to help Hilderbrand.  After several suggestions fell through due to their location or the high cost of installing water and sewer lines, someone proposed leasing the original property to her for one year while the village covers the utility hookups. Hilderbrand agreed, with the understanding she can keep looking for a permanent site and cancel the lease with 30 days’ notice. She will pay the village fifty dollars per month plus her own water, sewer, and electric costs. Trustees approved the agreement. The board called another special meeting for Monday, July 20 at 4:00 p.m., if Attorney Bright is available, to keep the project moving.

The mayor also mentioned that another person is interested in placing a modular home in Sunset Acres, but the board needs more information before making a decision.

Finally, trustees turned to the ongoing issue of nuisance properties. Attorney Bright said the Nuisance Committee should meet and create a list of targeted properties. He gave them a document outlining seven required steps. Bright agreed to contact the property owner and give them ten days to clean up. If they don’t comply, the village can take them to court, where owners could face up to $850 in fines and court costs. The board agreed to move forward with that approach, starting with the property at 225 South 4th Street SW. With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: DISASTER LOAN OUTREACH CENTERS
full_story:
The Illinois Emergency Management Agency and Office of Homeland Security, in partnership with the US Small Business Administration (SBA) and local municipalities, is promoting multiple Disaster Loan Outreach Centers (DLOCs) to assist residents and businesses impacted by the severe storms on June 10th, 11th and 17th.  These disaster declarations cover the primary counties of Cook and LaSalle for the June 10th, 11th storms and Coles and Effingham for the June 17th storms.  Residents and businesses in the contiguous counties are also eligible for SBA disaster assistance, including Clay, Clark, Cumberland, Douglas, Edgar, Fayette, Jasper, Moultrie, and Shelby Counties for the June 17th storms.  Centers will provide in person support for applicants seeking low interest disaster loans for storm related damages not covered by insurance.

SBA customer service representatives will staff each center to answer questions, explain the application process, and assist individuals and businesses in completing applications.  Walk-ins are welcome at all sites.  Residents and business owners in SBA declared disaster counties and counties that border those counties are eligible to apply and may visit any Disaster Loan Outreach Centers, regardless of where they live.

In Effingham County the Outreach Center will be at the Effingham School District Building at 2803 S. Banker St, and will be open Monday through Friday from 9:00 am to 6:00 pm and Saturday from 10:00 am to 2:00 pm.  For online applications, visit sba.gov/disaster.  Applicants may also call SBA’s Customer Service Center at 800-659-2955 or email [email protected].  People who are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability may dial 7-1-1 for relay services.

Homeowners can apply for up to $500,000 in low-interest SBA disaster loans to repair or replace damaged or destroyed real estate.  Homeowners or renters can apply for up to $100,000 to repair or replace damaged or destroyed personal property.  Businesses and not-for-profits can borrow up to $2 million for physical damages.  For more information, visit https://www.sba.gov/funding-programs/disaster-assistance.

In addition to the primary counties declared under this disaster, residents and businesses located in contiguous counties are also eligible to apply for SBA disaster assistance.  The deadline to submit SBA disaster loan applications for physical property damage is September 8th, and the deadline to submit applications for economic injury is April 12th, 2027.

title: NIEMERG APPOINTMENT
full_story:
State Representative Adam Niemerg has been appointed to serve on a special investigative committee convened to look into the federal charges State Representative Carol Ammons is facing.  Ammons has been indicted on charges of wire fraud, obtaining cash kickbacks from unlawful payments made from her campaign account, and taking payments from nonprofits (NGOs) that she helped receive state grant funding.

“This is a responsibility I do not take lightly,” Niemerg said.  “We must restore ethics, transparency and accountability in government and ensure the members of the General Assembly are leading by example.  This bipartisan committee to review the allegations is an important step forward, but we must not stop here.  We must pass meaningful ethics reforms to root out the culture of corruption in our state for good.”

In addition to Niemerg, other members of the Committee include Democrat Assistant Majority Leader Curtis J. Tarver II to chair the committee, along with Assistant Majority Leader Jay Hoffman, Rep. Lilian Jimenez.  On the Republican side, the Minority Leader Ryan Spain will serve as spokesman and Assistant Minority Leader Dan Ugaste was also appointed to the Committee.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
The results of an extended planting season are showing in fields across Illinois as both corn and soybeans exhibit a wide variety of growth stages.

In USDA’s latest crop progress and condition report, the department estimated 47% of soybeans were blooming, slightly behind last year and the five-year average pace. However, the number of fields setting pods was slightly ahead of average at 19%.

Corn silking reached 40%, with 6% in the dough stage, both slightly ahead of average.

The latest crop progress report was released on Monday.  According to the USDA there were 5.3 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending July 12th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 76.9 degrees, 1.3 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 1.27 inches, 0.31 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 2% very short, 8% short, 73% adequate, and 17% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 3% very short, 9% short, 73% adequate, and 15% surplus.

Corn silking reached 40%, compared to the 5-year average of 45%.  Corn reaching the dough stage is at 6% compared to the 5-year average of 4%.  Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 10% poor, 28% fair, 43% good, and 15% excellent.

Soybeans blooming reached 47%, compared to the 5-year average of 48%.  Soybeans setting pods reached 19% compared to the 5-year average of 12%.  Soybeans condition was rated 4% very poor, 10% poor, 30% fair, 44% good, and 12% excellent.

Winter wheat harvested for grain reached 88%, compared to the 5-year average of 93%.  Winter wheat condition was rated at 1% very poor, 9% poor, 33% fair, 52% good, and 5% excellent.

title: FAYETTE COUNTY SCAM
full_story:
The Fayette County Sheriff’s Office is warning the public of a scam involving an individual identifying themselves as a Deputy.

In a social media post, the Fayette County Sheriff’s Office says they have been made aware of a scam involving an individual identifying themselves as a Fayette County Deputy.  The individual claims he has a court order to “Make and Maintain Contact” and can not allow the caller to hang up until money has been deposited to take care of the warrant that has been issued by the Federal Government.  The individual is utilizing a “618” area code and is sending documents that appear to be legit.  If you have a warrant, a Fayette County Sheriff’s Deputy will personally come to your residence and take you to the Fayette County Jail and not to a bank as this individual is requesting.

The Fayette County Sheriff’s Office says they are currently working with Federal Authorities to identify this individual.

Please contact your local Law Enforcement if you have fallen victim to this scam.

title: GRILL RECALL
full_story:
The Consumer Product Safety Commission said thousands of grills sold online and at Walmart and Lowe’s stores nationally are being recalled.

Over 12-hundred stainless steel Cuisinart Propel+Four Burner three-in-one Gas Grills are included in the recall.  The units include a pizza oven with tempered glass that has reportedly shattered during use, causing a serious risk of injury from lacerations.  Conair LLC, has received 37 reports of glass shattering and one report of a fire.

To see if your grill is impacted, check the label on the inside of the right-hand metal door.  The recall is for grills with model number CGG-6331.  Grill owners should stop using the recalled grills immediately and visit the Conair website for instructions to safely remove the tempered glass window on the pizza oven and upload two photos, one of the removed glass and one of the grill’s serial numbers.  Consumers impacted by the recall may choose to be reimbursed for the original purchase amount or receive a 500 dollar refund by check.

title: IDNR ACCEPTING APPLICATIONS
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources is accepting applications for the State Pheasant Fund Special Funds and the Illinois Habitat Fund Special Funds Grant programs through August 1st.

The pheasant habitat and wildlife habitat programs enhance the natural environment for pheasant and wildlife through projects developed by not-for-profit organizations and governmental entities for conservation.  Funding for the State Pheasant Fund Special Funds and the Illinois Habitat Fund Special Wildlife Funds grants comes from the sale of habitat stamps to sportsmen and sportswomen.

Applicants must register and be current in the Grant Accountability and Transparency Act portal.  Applications must be submitted online.  For additional information, email [email protected].

View additional state funding opportunities by visiting the Illinois Catalog of Financial Assistance online.
